title: The Day of the Windblown Lists
skyStory: A slightly-over-half moon, fifty-three percent lit, is lounging in Aquarius and running an experiment on coincidence. It has written the same strange note twice and handed both copies to the gale. Saturn says this is unscientific. Mars says it is hilarious. The wind from the shore delivers the test materials personally, one gust at a time.

reading: Somewhere along your route today, a gust will slap a folded scrap of paper against your leg. It is somebody's to-do list in loopy blue pen: fix the weathervane, call the lighthouse, find the very small ladder. Take a photo. Then tuck it somewhere dry, in case its owner comes looking.

Here is the twist: Nancy will catch one too, within the same hour, different handwriting, same three chores. Neither of you will believe it at first. Don't even scream when the photos arrive side by side. The moon in Aquarius loves a pattern, and the [[Wheel of Fortune]] gets one spin today just to make you both laugh. ΔΕΣ, Tiger. Then wonder, seriously, how small that ladder is.
joel.mission: Photograph the most cheerful lost object you see today and caption it as if it were a famous explorer.
joel.omen: A scrap of paper tumbling uphill against the wind. The universe is reviewing your week favourably.

reading: The Wood Rat sees it first, of course: a scrap of paper pinned to a fence post by the gale, flapping like it wants your attention. You will unfold it and feel a funny prickle on the back of your neck, the Life Path 11 kind, the kind that means a story is about to happen.

Send the photo before you think too hard. When Joel's photo comes back with the very same list, tiny ladder and all, you will laugh so hard your hands do a whole interpretive dance. DES, Mountain. This is the sky reminding you that the two of you are tuned to the same channel, even across a gale. Save both pictures. They deserve a frame, or at least a folder.
nancy.mission: Leave a little note for a lost object you find today: 'Your human is looking for you. Stay put.'
nancy.omen: Handwriting that is not yours tucked somewhere it should not be. The other half of a pair is nearby, and it is a happy match.

together.text: Send each other the strangest matching thing you each see today, windblown lists included. Then invent the missing fourth chore together. If you both pick the same one, the moon wins its experiment and you owe it a respectful nod at moonrise. Keep the photos in a folder called Evidence.
